subject.title: [Feature]: Add TTL/Expiry for Delivery Queue Messages

question: What outbound delivery expiry policy should OpenClaw expose for queued delivery recovery: which config key, default behavior, and expired-entry action?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix adds public config/default behavior in a strict core schema and changes whether existing queued messages replay after upgrade, so automation should not choose that product contract alone.

options.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
options.body: Add an optional `messages.delivery.maxAgeMs` with a closed `expireAction` such as failed/quarantine, preserve current no-TTL default, and cover startup plus reconnect drains.

options.title: Finite default TTL
options.body: Ship a default max age to prevent stale floods without user setup, accepting a compatibility-sensitive change to existing recovery behavior.

options.title: Broader freshness design
options.body: Pause the outbound-only fix and design outbound plus inbound message freshness together, which may reduce drift but broadens the scope and delays the known outbound repair.

recommendation.title: Opt-in messages.delivery TTL
recommendation.body: Add an optional `messages.delivery.maxAgeMs` with a closed `expireAction` such as failed/quarantine, preserve current no-TTL default, and cover startup plus reconnect drains.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the delivery queue/config area and already gave maintainer-facing direction on this issue.
